$comment: P68 round 13 (lane `cs`, D-C-A-CONSTANT-ADDRESS-INITIALIZER-IS-REFUSED-AS-A-RUNTIME-INITIALIZER): the COMMA operator in a static initializer, which C 6.6p3 excludes from a constant expression — admitted because clang builds it (`semantics.staticInitializers.otherConstantForms: commaOperator`), WITH the diagnostic the constraint asks for (the two warnings expected below). MEASURED 2026-09-24 through `dssharness run probe-reference-cc` (lane `cs`'s batch runs 20260925-023301-54d7ccff on linux-x86_64-debug — gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 — and 20260925-023324-83d948e4 on windows-x86_64-debug — mingw-w64 13.2.0; AppleClang 21.0.0 on macos-arm64-release, run 20260925-030327-b1170b39, agrees with clang 18.1.3 throughout), this file at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors and at -std=c2x: clang exits 42 in both modes; gcc and mingw-w64 refuse it ("initializer element is not constant") — one working reference makes the form required; MSVC 19.51.36260 builds it too and exits 42 (/std:clatest and /std:c17; probe-reference-cc on windows-x86_64-release, run 20260925-101645-8038c787). The release arm is REPORT-ONLY (mustDifferFromBaseline false, on purpose): both values are folded into static data at compile time, so `main` has nothing the release pipeline transforms — the harness gate measured the release image byte-identical to the baseline (windows-x86_64-debug run 20260925-101508-45f3e186). exit 42 = both values are the last operand's.
